newsitem.title: USA: Rogers adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Rogers adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: Rogers Corp said it has adopted a new shareholders rights plan to replace one adopted in 1987 and will issue a dividend distribution of one right to purchase common stock of the company for each oustanding common share owned.
The company said its board also extended, through April 30, 1998, the authority of the company to buy up to $2 million in market value of its common stock.

Rogers said the shareholder rights plan is designed to assure that all shareholders receive fair and equal treatment in the event of a proposed takeover and to guard against partial tender offer or other abusive tactics to gain control of the company.

It said the rights plan does not prevent a takeover, but encourages negotiations with Rogers board should anyone seek to acquire the company. It also said the new rights plan was not adopted in response to any known effort to acquire the company.
